newsitem.title: USA: NASD penalizes brokers $1.8 mln for using imposter.
newsitem.headline: NASD penalizes brokers $1.8 mln for using imposter.

text.p: The National Association of Securities Dealers said Wednesday it barred, fined and censured 20 individuals suspected of paying an impostor to take a qualification examination on their behalf.
NASD Regulation, an arm of NASD, said the punishments stem from an investigation dating back to August 1996, when it became aware that prospective brokers were cheating to earn their licenses.
Each barred individual was required to forfeit his commissions, for a total of more than $1.2 million.
Individual fines included $25,000 for cheating on the examination and $25,000 if they failed to respond to NASD Regulation requests for information, for a total of $650,000.
"Every investor has the right to expect that their broker is honest and understands the securities markets and regulations," said NASD Regulation president Mary L. Schapiro.
"These entrance exams are a cornerstone of NASD Regulation's investor-protection framework."
